findings.location: README.md L67 and the package root
findings.evidence: The README names FinalAnalysis_ECOLAPP_Schubert.et.al.R as the analysis code for this manuscript. That file is not in the archive. The only R file present declares in its first line that it reproduces the Applied Vegetation Science manuscript.
findings.impact: Blocks independent verification of every inferential result, including rarefied richness and its confidence intervals, sampling completeness, NMDS, PERMANOVA, and all model-based comparisons in Figure 3.
findings.severity_basis: Tested by claim coverage: 7 of 50 ledger claims, comprising all inferential claims, cannot be evaluated.
findings.author_question: Could you supply FinalAnalysis_ECOLAPP_Schubert.et.al.R, which the README lists but which is not present in the archive?

findings.evidence: The sentence states that of the naturally recruited taxa, 94.2% of individuals were identified to species, 4.6% to genus and 1.1% to family. The genus figure matches taxon counts exactly at 12 of 261, or 4.60%. At individual level the genus share is 0.21%.
findings.impact: Descriptive only. The stated percentages are correct as taxon proportions, and the word individuals is the error. No downstream analysis depends on it.
findings.severity_basis: Tested: an exact taxon-level match was found and the individual-level value differs by a factor of about 22. No analytic result depends on this sentence.
findings.reviewer_action: Ask for the wording to be corrected to taxa.
findings.author_question: Should the phrase of individuals read of taxa? The reported percentages match taxon counts rather than individual counts.

findings.evidence: The manuscript reports that approximately 50% of mid-successional and 15% of late-successional species were recorded in the tree size class of any restoration treatment. The mid-successional figure recomputes to exactly 50.0%, or 26 of 52. The late-successional figure recomputes to 21.3%, or 35 of 164, and to 21.0% on the retained set.
findings.impact: Not evaluated. The exact match on the companion figure in the same sentence indicates the interpretation is correct, but the effect of the late-successional difference on any conclusion was not tested.
findings.severity_basis: UNDETERMINED. The discrepancy is demonstrated, but its effect was not evaluated.
findings.reviewer_action: Ask how the late-successional percentage was derived.
findings.author_question: How was the 15% figure for late-successional species in the tree size class calculated? The same calculation reproduces the companion 50% figure exactly but yields about 21% here.

findings.evidence: The manuscript reports that 60% of planted-species sapling stems in the two planted treatments were originally-planted individuals. The recomputed value is 65.3%, or 126 of 193.
findings.impact: A difference of 5.3 percentage points. The direction and the qualitative statement that a majority were originally planted are unaffected.
findings.severity_basis: Tested: recomputed on the full sapling set, and the majority claim holds under both values.
findings.author_question: Which denominator produced 60%? Counting all planted-species saplings in applied nucleation and plantation gives 65.3%.

findings.evidence: The manuscript states that all trees of at least 5 cm DBH of these species in applied nucleation and plantation were planted as part of the initial restoration. The dataset records 17 such stems coded as recruits: 11 in applied nucleation, comprising 4 Erythrina poeppigiana and 7 Inga edulis, and 6 in plantation, comprising 4 E. poeppigiana, 1 I. edulis and 1 Vochysia guatemalensis, spanning 5.0 to 27.3 cm DBH.
findings.impact: 17 of 1,781 such stems, or 0.95%. The quantitative pattern is unaffected and only the universal quantifier is contradicted.
findings.severity_basis: Tested: affected stems were counted against the full set, giving 17 of 1,781, or 0.95%.
findings.reviewer_action: Ask for the word all to be qualified.
findings.author_question: The data record 17 recruit-origin stems of the planted species at 5 cm DBH or above in these treatments. Should the statement be qualified?

findings.evidence: The manuscript reports an 18.6% early-successional share of plantation saplings. The recomputed value is 18.19% using all records or 18.52% using recruits only. The companion natural regeneration and applied nucleation figures in the same sentence reproduce exactly, at 53.95% and 43.30%, under the all-records rule, which yields 18.19% for plantation.
findings.impact: At most 0.41 percentage points. Treatment ordering and the qualitative contrast are unaffected.
findings.severity_basis: Tested across four denominator rules, with a maximum deviation of 0.41 percentage points and ordering preserved in every variant.
findings.reviewer_action: Ask which rule was applied, noting that no single rule reproduces all three values in the sentence.
findings.author_question: No single inclusion rule reproduces all three sapling percentages in this sentence. Which rule was used for the plantation value?

findings.evidence: The manuscript reports that 64% of mid-successional species have small seeds under 5 mm. The recomputed value is 69.2%, or 36 of 52, from the census trait fields and identically from the 2025 trait master. The companion figure in the same sentence, 71% of late-successional species with seeds of at least 5 mm, reproduces at 71.1%.
findings.impact: A difference of 5.2 percentage points, equivalent to 3 species of 52. The stated qualitative conclusion that most mid-successional species have small seeds holds under both values.
findings.severity_basis: Tested against both supplied trait sources. The companion figure in the same sentence reproduces, which argues against systematic trait-table drift.
findings.reviewer_action: Ask for the mid-successional figure to be rechecked.
findings.author_question: Both trait sources give 69.2%, or 36 of 52, rather than 64%, while the companion 71% figure reproduces exactly. Could the 64% value be rechecked?

findings.evidence: The manuscript reports that 0.04% of individuals were not identified and were excluded. Candidate definitions give 0.030%, or 26 individuals in the six poor-resolution taxa, and 0.100%, or 86 individuals whose Family field is blank. A value of 0.04% would correspond to about 34 individuals, and no tested definition yields that.
findings.impact: Not material to any analysis. The excluded fraction is negligible under every definition tested.
findings.severity_basis: Tested across four candidate definitions of not identified. All fall outside the reported value, but the absolute quantity is negligible in every case.
findings.reviewer_action: Ask which records were treated as unidentified.
findings.author_question: Which records were counted as not identified? Candidate definitions give 0.030% or 0.100% rather than 0.04%.

findings.evidence: The area file lists 33 plots including BBPL with 243 quadrats, but BBPL has no records in the census file and the manuscript reports 8 plantation plots. A naive join of the two files would inflate plantation sampled area from 1.8108 to 2.0295 hectares, an increase of 12.1%.
findings.impact: Tested and found not to have propagated. The reported later-successional tree density ratio of 8% reproduces at exactly 8.0% only when BBPL is excluded, and gives 7.7% if it is included. This is positive evidence that the published analysis used the correct eight-plot set.
findings.severity_basis: Tested: the discrepancy is a reuse hazard in the archive rather than an error in the published result.
findings.reviewer_action: Ask for BBPL to be removed or flagged in the archived file.
findings.author_question: PlotQuadrantes.csv contains a BBPL row with no corresponding census records. Should it be removed or flagged so that reusers do not join it into area calculations?

findings.evidence: The census file is Latin-1 encoded, which the README does not state, and a standard UTF-8 read fails at byte 137401. The seed_size column contains two undocumented codes, UNK with 16 records and a question mark with 1 record. Five taxa have a blank Family field, covering 86 individuals.
findings.impact: Affects reuse rather than the reported results. No published value depends on these defects.
findings.severity_basis: Tested: each defect was reproduced directly and none propagates to a reported value.
findings.reviewer_action: Ask for the encoding and the missing-value codes to be documented.
findings.author_question: Could the README state the file encoding and define the UNK and question-mark codes in seed_size?

findings.evidence: The supplied PDF is a 38-page accepted-manuscript postprint containing no embedded images on any page and no supplementary material.
findings.impact: All figure-level and supplement-level claims are unverifiable from what was supplied. This is a limitation of the review materials rather than a defect of the published article.
findings.severity_basis: Tested: image extraction returned zero images across all 38 pages.
findings.reviewer_action: Obtain the typeset article and supplement.
findings.author_question: Not applicable, because this concerns the materials supplied to the audit.

corrections_to_prior_run.prior_statement: seed_size is stored in mixed string and float formats, putting 1,308 records at risk of silent category splitting
corrections_to_prior_run.basis: Raw token inspection with the standard library CSV reader shows only the values 1, 2, 3, NA, UNK and a question mark. The decimal-formatted tokens appear only under the chunked type inference used by a default pandas read and are an artifact of the reader, not a property of the file.

corrections_to_prior_run.prior_statement: Richness values of 156, 185, 196 and 205 do not reproduce; recomputed 155, 184, 195 and 204
corrections_to_prior_run.basis: Reported richness equals retained richness plus one in all four treatments. The rule discriminates, because applied nucleation contains three excluded taxa yet still gains only one, which rules out per-taxon reinstatement. The manuscript documents grouping of inconsistently identified taxa for diversity analyses at p.11 L217-218.

corrections_to_prior_run.prior_statement: 65 families reported but only 64 present in the data
corrections_to_prior_run.basis: 64 named families plus one unassigned group equals the reported 65, consistent with the same documented grouping rule.

corrections_to_prior_run.prior_statement: The claim of all but 10.5% does not reproduce; recomputed 13.24% absent
corrections_to_prior_run.basis: The prior figure used all size classes, whereas the manuscript states tree species. Restricting to reference-forest tree species gives 10.34% to 10.96% absent, which brackets the reported 10.5%, and the companion statement of about 90% of reference forest species also reproduces, at 89.0%.

corrections_to_prior_run.prior_statement: The Figure 1 caption value of 163 late-successional species does not reproduce; recomputed 162
corrections_to_prior_run.basis: 162 retained plus one grouped unit equals 163, which is the same rule that reconciles the richness values.

corrections_to_prior_run.prior_statement: The values 7.7%, 79.1% and 70.6% were recorded as reported manuscript values that matched exactly
corrections_to_prior_run.basis: None of these strings occurs in the manuscript. They were the prior run's own recomputed values entered in the reported-value column. The actual manuscript claims are 8%, more than 75%, and 71%, which recompute to 8.0%, 79.1% and 71.1% respectively and are confirmed.

corrections_to_prior_run.prior_statement: BBPL inflates plantation area, with the effect recorded as UNDETERMINED
corrections_to_prior_run.basis: The 8% density claim reproduces at exactly 8.0% only when BBPL is excluded, which demonstrates that the published analysis used the correct eight-plot set. The archive defect remains a reuse hazard and is retained as F-09.

corrections_to_prior_run.prior_statement: The Methods state 37 early-successional species, conflicting with the Figure 1 caption value of 38
corrections_to_prior_run.basis: The string could not be located in this extraction of the manuscript. It is recorded as C-49 NOT_CHECKED rather than asserted as a finding.

verdict_scope.checked_subset: All descriptive and derived numerical claims recoverable from the supplied census, area and trait files. No inferential result was checked.
verdict_scope.why_not_matches: Coverage excludes every model-based result, so the domain is not broad enough to support MATCHES or MINOR_DISCREPANCIES.
